 Gov. Braun Urges Veterans to Claim Property Tax Relief Before Deadline
 The deadline for Hoosier veterans to get property tax relief is January 15, 2027.
 Written by 
 Jarett Lewis 
 Published on 
 November 16, 2026 
 Comments
 Share 
 Share the post 
 Share this link via
 Or copy link
 Copy 
 Copied 
 Indiana Gov. Mike Braun (Source: Office of Governor Mike Braun) 
 INDIANAPOLIS — Indiana Gov. Mike Braun is reminding veterans about an upcoming deadline to claim property tax relief.
 In a video released on Monday, Gov. Braun and Indiana Department of Veterans Affairs Director Jake Adams urged Hoosier veterans to take advantage of expanded property tax relief before the deadline on Jan. 15, 2027.
 “If you’re a disabled veteran, there are property tax savings that we want you to know about,” the governor said.
 Earlier this year, Gov. Braun signed legislation that eliminated property taxes on primary residences for totally disabled veterans and extended property tax credits to more than 50,000 additional veterans and their surviving spouses.
 “These credits are stackable, meaning Hoosier veterans can receive a larger overall benefit than ever before,” Braun said. “I will always prioritize ensuring more of your money stays in your own pocket.”
 Veterans are encouraged to contact their local veteran service officers to see whether they qualify and to apply.
